headline: Pet spending holds pricing power and margin even as consumers trade down elsewhere.

deltas.to: Q1 2026 gross margin 30.1%, +50 basis points YoY; nearly 200,000 net customer additions
deltas.change: +50 bps margin expansion YoY, +7.7% net sales
deltas.reads: Pet parents sustained autoship and pharmacy spending despite more dynamic consumer backdrop; volume and margin both rising

deltas.metric: metal container demand for pet food
deltas.to: Q4 2025: 7% growth in metal containers for pet-food markets
deltas.reads: Pet-food packaging outpacing broader rigid-container growth, signaling outsized category demand

deltas.metric: Hill's Pet Nutrition resilience relative to personal care
deltas.to: Q2 2026: management explicit statement that Hill's spending more resilient to affordability pressure than personal care
deltas.change: category-relative pricing power confirmed in filings
deltas.reads: Pet nutrition holds pricing floor when consumers cut back on hygiene trade-ups; dependency protection visible

deltas.from: Q4 FY26: same-store sales up 1.3% FY26
deltas.to: Q1 FY27: same-store sales up 1.8%, AUR up 5%, positive Valentine's and Mother's Day
deltas.reads: Emotionally coded gifting and milestone spending remains durable; similar consumer-identity mechanism as pet parenthood

deltas.metric: emotional participation and commemoration (adjacent to pet parenthood identity)
deltas.to: Q1 2026 pre-tax income $23.9M before tariff benefits, commercial/franchise up 34.1%
deltas.change: core DTC softened but emotional-commerce channel diversification deepened
deltas.reads: Ceremony-based spending still commands loyalty and capital allocation even when traffic softens; identity attachment holds

deltas.metric: active customer base and Autoship penetration
deltas.to: Q1 2026: nearly 200,000 net new customers added; autoship architecture implicit in margin expansion
deltas.reads: Pet parents treating pet care as non-discretionary recurring expense; repeat behavior and account stickiness deepening

momentum_note: The pet economy is accelerating as a resilience category. Chewy expanded both margin and customer base in a quarter management called dynamic, while Silgan saw outsize pet-food container growth and Colgate explicitly flagged Hill's Pet Nutrition as more resilient to affordability pressure than personal care. The mechanism is identity protection: pet parents treat pet spending as non-negotiable before cutting discretionary personal care or gifting. This resembles how emotionally coded spending in weddings (Signet) and participation ceremonies (Build-A-Bear) holds up even when broader consumer signals weaken. The pricing floor is behavioral, not market-driven.
